consensus_findings.description: Round two's blocker 3 was fixed in the payload but not in the durable decision that justifies it, so the D1 trace is now false in exactly the way the round-two D5 trace was. session-log.md:11 records the Implementation decision as `**Use portable canonical guide links** `architectural: skill-workflow` -- Installed skill payloads cannot use relative links that escape the skill directory; a stable repository URL remains clickable in canonical and mirrored copies.` No stable repository URL exists anywhere in the branch any more: all six sources now carry the bare backticked path (`grep -rn state-artifacts skills/**/SKILL.md` returns the identical sentence at skills/autopilot/SKILL.md:17, skills/autopilot-roadmap/SKILL.md:16, skills/session-log/SKILL.md:15, skills/supervise/SKILL.md:17, skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md:22, skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md:22), and the test constant was renamed accordingly from `GUIDE_LINK` to `GUIDE_REFERENCE = "docs/guides/state-artifacts.md"` (test_state_artifacts_guide.py:16). A repo-wide grep for `github.com/jankneumann/agentic-coding-tools/blob/main/docs/guides/state-artifacts` outside `reviews/` returns nothing. The decision's own title is also now inaccurate -- a bare backticked path is a reference, not a link, and nothing rendered is clickable. The consequence is worse than a stale sentence because docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md:12 carries the same text verbatim: that file is generated by `PhaseRecord.write_both()` step four, which skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:355-372 documents as running 'last, and unconditionally' precisely because 'a session-log entry is the only thing that invalidates that index'. So the capability timeline -- the artifact every future skill-workflow change inherits its conventions from -- now publishes a rationale for a URL convention this branch deliberately abandoned, and hand-editing the generated file would be overwritten on the next session-log write.

CI test discovery resolution: `skills/pyproject.toml` registers `tests/state-artifacts` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options].testpaths` (line 129). `test_ci_test_coverage.py` passes completely without exemption, ensuring `skills/tests/state-artifacts/test_state_artifacts_guide.py` is executed during CI pytest runs.

Safe runtime mirror assertion handling: `test_changed_skill_mirrors_are_byte_identical` in `skills/tests/state-artifacts/test_state_artifacts_guide.py` (lines 86-87) safely executes `pytest.skip()` when `.agents/skills` or `.claude/skills` directory mirrors are absent, preventing `FileNotFoundError` exceptions during uninstalled test execution while retaining byte-identity verification when mirrors exist.

Portable repository guide reference convention: `skills/autopilot/SKILL.md` (and all five other updated skill files `autopilot-roadmap`, `session-log`, `supervise`, `implement-feature`, `validate-feature`) references `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md` using the repo-relative backtick convention rather than hardcoding remote main branch GitHub URLs, matching codebase conventions established by work-queue-truth-projection.md and memory-conventions.md.

Eight-step rehydration algorithm alignment across design, supervise, and canonical guide: `design.md` (lines 39-46), `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md` (lines 21-28), and `skills/supervise/SKILL.md` (lines 139-153) share the exact 8-step rehydration sequence (1. Bootstrap locator, 2. Roadmap definition, 3. Roadmap execution state, 4. Change execution state, 5. Learning context, 6. Phase history, 7. Handoff context, 8. Rebuild projections). Additionally, D5 in `design.md` and `change-context.md` accurately permits the generated `docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md` decision index as a derived projection.

Writer ordering accuracy: `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md` line 40 explicitly enumerates decision-index regeneration as the fourth step of `PhaseRecord.write_both()`, matching the exact runtime behavior in `skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py`.

The three documents do now share the same eight-step algorithm in prose -- design.md:39-46, docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:21-28 and skills/supervise/SKILL.md:138-153 all run Bootstrap locator, Roadmap definition, Roadmap execution state, Change execution state, Learning context, Phase history, Handoff context, Rebuild projections, with design.md's former seven-step form (the round-two nit that merged roadmap.yaml and checkpoint.json into one bullet, and cited 'steps 2-3' for handoff consistency) corrected to eight steps citing 'steps 2-4'. But the drift guard pins that agreement asymmetrically. `test_guide_pins_rehydration_order_and_conflict_rules` (lines 43-54) checks all eight markers against the guide, while `test_supervise_rehydration_matches_canonical_order` (lines 68-78) enumerates only seven: 'Rebuild projections' is absent from the tuple. Supervise's step 8 -- 'Derive queue and display state from the verified canonical records, never the reverse' -- is the one that carries the truth/projection invariant the whole change inherits from ri-07, and it can be deleted, or moved above step 7, with the suite still green. design.md's own eight-step listing is pinned by no test at all, so the artifact that defines the algorithm is the only one of the three free to drift.

Round two's blocker 2 is genuinely fixed -- test_state_artifacts_guide.py:86-87 now calls `pytest.skip` when either mirror is absent, so a fresh checkout no longer raises FileNotFoundError from `.read_bytes()` -- but the plan artifacts have not absorbed what that means for enforcement. .gitignore:280-281 excludes `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, `git ls-files .agents/skills .claude/skills` returns nothing, and the only CI step that touches the payload is `bash install.sh --check` at .github/workflows/ci.yml:65, which skills/install.sh:40 documents as 'Validate the complete install payload and exit without syncing'. No CI job runs install.sh in sync mode. So in CI the six mirror cases always skip: the spec scenario 'Runtime skill mirrors are installed' (specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:46-49) has no enforcing check anywhere except a developer machine that happens to have run install.sh -- which is what I confirmed locally, where md5sum shows skills/, .agents/skills/ and .claude/skills/ identical for supervise and session-log. change-context.md:12 still records the evidence unqualified as 'Focused GREEN: 15 passed' and 'Six parametrized cases; 12 byte comparisons when mirrors are installed' (the count itself is now correct, resolving the round-two arithmetic complaint), and design.md:57 states the mitigation as a manual 'run skills/install.sh and byte-compare' step. Nothing states that the CI outcome for this module is 9 passed / 6 skipped and that mirror parity is therefore an unenforced local convention.

Round two's blocker 1 is resolved at the mechanism level: skills/pyproject.toml now lists `tests/state-artifacts` in testpaths (between `tests/codebase-atlas` and `expedite/scripts/tests`), the .github/workflows/ci.yml `test-infra-skills` job runs with `working-directory: skills` and executes `uv run pytest -v` with no path argument at line 70, and skills/tests/ci_coverage/test_ci_test_coverage.py `_covered()` unions `_testpaths()` with the ci.yml arguments, so `test_directory_is_reached_by_ci[tests/state-artifacts]` resolves. The file is also correctly inside scope -- work-packages.yaml lists skills/pyproject.toml in both locks.files:44 and scope.write_allow:61. What did not follow is the plan record. No task in tasks.md instructs the registration: 1.1 says only 'Add the structural contract test at skills/tests/state-artifacts/test_state_artifacts_guide.py' and its Coverage field enumerates assertions; 3.2 was updated to run 'the CI test-coverage guard' but naming the verification is not the same as owning the edit. Neither does the change-context.md traceability matrix -- its 'Files Changed' column names docs/guides/state-artifacts.md, docs/guides/documentation.md, six SKILL.md files and the mirrors, but never skills/pyproject.toml, so the requirement 'the drift guard this change creates actually executes in CI' has no Req ID, no mapped test, and no evidence row. The same omission applies to docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md, which appears in the diff and in scope but only in the Design Decision Trace D5 row, not in the requirement matrix.

The inserted sentence carries a stray definite article before the backticked path: 'Shared holder, writer, authority, fallback, and rehydration semantics live in the `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md`.' The convention this change correctly adopted writes the path without one -- skills/coordination-bridge/SKILL.md:81 ('`docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md`. The invariant is guarded by'), skills/vision/SKILL.md:116 ('Full rules: `docs/guides/worktree-management.md`'), and skills/session-log/SKILL.md:155 ('See `docs/guides/memory-conventions.md` for the full tag schema'). The identical sentence is duplicated verbatim across all six canonical sources and both runtime mirrors, so the wording is copied eighteen times; fixing it later costs an install.sh resync. Purely editorial: the test asserts on the substring `docs/guides/state-artifacts.md`, which is unaffected either way.

Verified independently against the runtime rather than against the spec text: every inventory row resolves to a real writer. Roadmap checkpoint -> skills/roadmap-runtime/scripts/checkpoint.py:39 sets `self.checkpoint_path = workspace / 'checkpoint.json'` inside CheckpointManager, matching the guide's `openspec/roadmaps/<roadmap-id>/checkpoint.json` holder. Phase record -> `PhaseRecord.write_both()` at skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:355. Handoff document -> the local fallback under `openspec/changes/<change-id>/handoffs/` and the supervisor mirror `openspec/supervise/supervisor-record.json`, both named in the same row. The queue exclusion at line 15 ('The coordinator work queue is a derived projection, not a sixth authority class') points at docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md, which exists and is the same target skills/coordination-bridge/SKILL.md:81 cites, so the projection boundary has one destination rather than two. All six required columns are present in the header row and each of the five classes states missing/stale behavior with the first-run case carved out explicitly ('Absence is valid before the run starts', 'Absence is valid for a never-started roadmap').

Supervise is the one of the six skills where prose was genuinely replaced rather than only appended (16 deletions against 30 insertions; the other five are pure +4 additions of the pointer block, which is correct because their remaining loop-state references are phase-specific mutation commands the plan explicitly preserves). The replacement keeps bootstrap and verification separated at both ends: step 1 constrains the locator -- 'This selects the newer valid handoff or mirror only as a locator' -- and step 7 closes it -- 'canonical state wins even when the handoff is newer'. Step 3 carries the first-run carve-out operationally ('Absence is valid only for a never-started roadmap; a resume claim without it is degraded and stops automatic advancement') and step 4 forbids reconstruction ('Never reconstruct a missing or invalid loop state from the supervisor record'), which is the ri-09 failure proposal.md:7 cites. Nothing operational was lost in the compression: the `try_handoff_read(limit=1, supervisor_only=true)` call, the cycle_state.py rehydrate command, the `Degraded: handoff` report and the cycle-ledger.json read all survive inside the new step structure. The guide reference itself now matches repository convention -- a bare backticked repo-relative path, which is payload-safe without depending on a hostname and is not a relative link that would trip skills/shared/validate_install_manifest.py.

Package DAG, scope and validation weight all check out for a documentation-only surface. One package, `depends_on: []` (line 38), so there is no cycle, no cross-package overlap and no scheduler ordering question -- design.md:49-50 states the reason (concurrent edits to six shared SKILL.md files carrying an identical block would conflict for no throughput gain). All ten `locks.files` entries reappear in `scope.write_allow`, so nothing is locked-but-unwritable or writable-but-unlocked. `write_allow` enumerates exact paths, using globs only where a directory is the genuine unit (`skills/tests/state-artifacts/**`, the change directory), honouring the design.md:50 prohibition on repository-wide write globs; `deny` blocks agent-coordinator/src/**, agent-coordinator/database/** and apps/**, consistent with the proposal's Non-Goals. The `context_impact.surfaces` list now declares `decisions` alongside `documentation` and `semantic_code`, which is the validator-required counterpart to docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md being in scope. Verification is two commands producing exactly the two result_keys `outputs.result_keys` declares, at tier B, with security/deploy/browser recorded N/A at design.md:66 -- proportionate given the product diff is Markdown plus one dependency-free test module.

No new authentication, authorization, input-validation, deserialization or secret-handling surface is introduced, and the contracts declaration says so accurately rather than by omission: 'No OpenAPI, database, event, or generated-type contract applies.' Confirmed against the change's own commit range (e8019bfb~1..HEAD), which touches only Markdown, JSON/YAML plan artifacts, one TOML testpaths line and one test module -- no agent-coordinator source, no migration, no HTTP surface. The one new executable file reads files and compares strings; it imports pathlib and pytest and nothing else. Skipping the security-review phase is the correct call here rather than a deferred obligation.

Two round-two items verified fixed in this file and its downstream trace. D5 now permits the generated index explicitly -- 'The generated `docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md` index remains an allowed derived projection and is regenerated by the standard phase-record writer' -- which removes the contradiction with the branch diff, and change-context.md:22 was updated in step ('D5 - No hand-authored ADR | Generated decision index is allowlisted as a derived projection'), so the design decision, the trace row and the work-package scope now agree. The scope reconciliation at plan-findings.md:37 keeps the granularity right by naming the single derived file rather than opening docs/decisions/**. Separately, the guide's Writer ordering paragraph (docs/guides/state-artifacts.md:40) now names the fourth step -- 'and then regenerates the derived capability decision index' -- which I confirmed against the runtime docstring at skills/session-log/scripts/phase_record.py:356-372: 'Best-effort 4-step persistence: markdown -> sanitize -> coordinator -> regenerate the decision index', with step four documented as running 'last, and unconditionally'. Guide and implementation now describe the same four steps in the same order, which is what the guide's own closing rule at line 44 demands.

FYI: work-packages.yaml context_impact.surfaces now includes decisions alongside documentation and semantic_code, but context-checkpoints/wp-state-artifacts-docs.json and change-context.md Implementation Evidence still report declared surfaces as only documentation and semantic_code. Task 3.2 remains unchecked, so this is stale validation evidence rather than a missing package declaration.

Round-2 CI discovery blocker is resolved: skills/pyproject.toml testpaths includes tests/state-artifacts (line 129), the directory is in package locks/write_allow, default pytest --collect-only from skills/ collects all 15 state-artifacts tests, and skills/tests/ci_coverage/test_ci_test_coverage.py passes for tests/state-artifacts.

Round-2 guide-reference convention blocker is resolved: GUIDE_REFERENCE is docs/guides/state-artifacts.md; all six canonical skills reference that exact bare path in backticks; no blob/main GitHub URL remains; specs/skill-workflow/spec.md scenario requires the same path string.

Round-2 writer-ordering gap is resolved: docs/guides/state-artifacts.md Writer ordering now states PhaseRecord.write_both() appends and sanitizes, attempts coordinator handoff with local fallback, and then regenerates the derived capability decision index — matching phase_record.py's documented 4-step pipeline (markdown → sanitize → coordinator → regenerate).

design.md Rehydration Algorithm, docs/guides/state-artifacts.md Canonical rehydration order, and skills/supervise/SKILL.md Rehydrate steps 1–8 share the exact titles Bootstrap locator, Roadmap definition, Roadmap execution state, Change execution state, Learning context, Phase history, Handoff context, Rebuild projections; guide+supervise tests pin ordered markers (supervise retains cycle-ledger as local detail inside step 2, consistent with round-1 disposition).

Package DAG/scope remain valid: single package wp-state-artifacts-docs with depends_on []; validate_work_packages.py reports VALID; every locks.files entry is in write_allow; deny blocks agent-coordinator/src/**, database/**, and apps/**; openspec validate --strict passes.

RED/GREEN validity holds: validation/red-state-artifacts.md records 9 failed/6 passed before the guide; focused suite now yields 15 passed; assertions remain structural (five class names, five table headers, eight ordered markers, GUIDE_REFERENCE, optional mirror byte-identity) per design.md D4.

Fail-loud missing-state behavior is specified consistently: guide distinguishes first-run absence from claimed-progress inconsistency, supervise steps 3–4 stop automatic advancement when checkpoint/loop-state are missing under a resume claim, and inventory writers resolve to real runtime paths (save_state, checkpoint helpers, learning writer, write_both, supervisor MIRROR_PATH).

Validation remains proportional to a documentation-only surface: design.md marks security/deploy/browser N/A; contracts/README.md declares no OpenAPI/DB/event contracts; verification tier B runs focused pytest skills/tests/state-artifacts plus openspec validate --strict and validate_work_packages.py; task 3.2's fuller matrix stays pending hygiene rather than inventing runtime gates.

No new auth, input-validation, secret-handling, or network surface is introduced; proposal Non-Goals confine the change to documenting existing artifacts plus repository-local structural tests, and package deny keeps coordinator source and apps out of write scope.
